mechanism_evidence.contract: __finalize__ propagates attrs by deepcopy: the new object owns an independent attrs mapping; nested attrs values are not (is not) the originals; mutating the copy leaves the original untouched; captured at the copy/finalize timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Deepcopy a DataFrame carrying nested attrs, then mutate the copy.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Shallow per-key assignment shares nested attrs objects between original and copy.

discriminating_observation.description:
import copy
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [2, 3]})
df.attrs["tags"] = {"spam", "ham"}
result = copy.deepcopy(df)
print("attrs_identity", result.attrs["tags"] is df.attrs["tags"])
assert result.attrs["tags"] is not df.attrs["tags"]
result.attrs["tags"].add("eggs")
print("orig_untouched", df.attrs["tags"])
assert df.attrs["tags"] == {"spam", "ham"}
print("f2_attrs_isolation", True)

triple.shared_mutation_visibility: mutating the copy's nested attrs leaves the original's attrs untouched

mechanism_evidence.contract: Each sampled patch owns deep copies of the unmodified input keys: sample entries are not (is not) the input objects nor shared across samples; changing one sample leaves others and the input untouched; captured at the transform __call__ timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Sample multiple patches sharing unmodified keys, then mutate one sample.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Shallow assignment shares input objects across all samples; changing one changes all.

mechanism_evidence.contract: _ReprClass singletons (e.g. _UNDEFINED) preserve identity across copy and deepcopy: copies are identical (is) to the original, so existing is/is-not comparisons keep working; captured at the copy/deepcopy call timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Copy or deepcopy an object holding a _ReprClass constant.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Default copy/deepcopy duplicates the constant; cpf.bar is _UNDEFINED fails.

discriminating_observation.description:
import copy

f = Foo()
cpf = copy.deepcopy(f)
print("deepcopy_identity", cpf.bar is _UNDEFINED)
assert cpf.bar is _UNDEFINED
print("f2_singleton_identity", True)

mechanism_evidence.contract: Inherited hooks are per-instance copies: a derived instance hook is not (is not) the base hook object (same stamp for ordering); registering/deactivating on the derived side leaves the base side untouched; captured at hook-decoration/inheritance timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Register a hook in a derived class; base-class hooks must survive.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Derived registration reuses the base hook objects; base hooks get wiped.

discriminating_observation.description:
from openmdao.utils.hooks import _HookMeta
calls = []
base = _HookMeta("C", None, lambda inst: calls.append("base"))
child = base.copy()
print("hook_identity", child is base)
assert child is not base
assert child._stamp == base._stamp
child.deactivate()
base(None)
assert calls == ["base"]
print("f2_hook_isolation", True)

triple.is_identity: child hook is not base hook (same stamp)
triple.shared_mutation_visibility: deactivating the child leaves the base hook callable

mechanism_evidence.contract: copy/deepcopy of observable collections preserve observable wiring: the copy is a new object (is not the original) sharing the same _parent linkage (is the original parent); deepcopy isolates nested items while shallow copy shares them; captured at the copy call timepoint.
mechanism_evidence.trigger: Copy/deepcopy an ObservableDict/ObservableList nested in observed storage.
mechanism_evidence.base_wrong_behavior: Default deepcopy duplicates wiring metadata by value, dropping parent linkage (data loss on writeback).
mechanism_evidence.causal_change: __copy__/__deepcopy__ rebuild the same observable type with the same _parent.
